newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa turns up late to end at day's highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa turns up late to end at day's highs.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures turned higher on light, scattered buying in the last hour of trade to end up at session highs on Tuesday.

May closed up three stg at 1,006 stg per tonne. July recovered from the lowest level since April 10 to end up three at 1,024. Total volume stood at 4,367 contracts, with July leading by notching 1,048 contracts.
The late buying helped cocoa erase earlier losses when crosses and origins' against actuals (AAs) dominated trade. Origins were seen mostly hedging in back months.
July 1997/March 1998 and July 1998/March 1998 switches were most active in the morning.
Traders were neither excited nor disappointed with cocoa's performance. Most still saw July in a broad range between the April 2 high of 1,065 and support between 990 and the April 9 low of 980.
Until July breaks out on either side, they expected cocoa to vascillate in this range amid light to moderate volume.
But some traders said a July close below a bearish trendline near the 15-day moving average around 1,010 and 1,012 would mean Others said a break of 987 would likely draw in fund selling.
On the other side, a sharp move toward resistance at 1,065 could trigger buy-stops.
Steady Ivorian cocoa product exports and a rise in bean exports in February versus January had little impact on prices.

News the Ivory Coast is destroying some cocoa farms in its protected forests came out after the close. But crop analysts and forest officials in Abidjan said the impact of the move on the 1996/97 (October-September) output would be minimal as officials awaited clear eviction plans.
In options, 10 July 1,100 stg calls traded, according to LIFFE.
